cards.explanation: The answer is their own transgression and sins. God says to declare “…to My people their transgression and to the house of Jacob their sins.” (Isaiah 58:1) So the loud voice points at His own people, not off in the distance. I think that's the hardest kind of volume to use, friends, because nobody wants the big announcement to be about them.

The answer is True. God says “They ask Me for righteous judgments; they delight in the nearness of God.” (Isaiah 58:2) So on the surface these people look serious about God. That's why what comes next in the chapter lands so hard, friends.

The answer is oppress. God says “…on the day of your fast, you do as you please, and you oppress all your workers.” (Isaiah 58:3) The fast is happening and the workers are getting squeezed on the very same day. I'd have a hard time calling that a day of humbling, friends.

The answer is False. God says, “You cannot fast as you do today and have your voice be heard on high.” (Isaiah 58:4) A fast tangled up in contention and strife doesn't get their voice heard on high. Cannot means cannot, friends.

The answer is that it's not His chosen fast. After asking about the bowed head, sackcloth and ashes, He turns around and says what His chosen fast is: “to break the chains of wickedness, to untie the cords of the yoke, to set the oppressed free and tear off every yoke?” (Isaiah 58:6) So the question steers them away from the show and toward something else. Sackcloth is a rough cloth, friends, but He's after more than what a person wears.

The answer is that it tears off every yoke. God's chosen fast is to “…set the oppressed free and tear off every yoke?” (Isaiah 58:6) Every single one, friends. He's not talking about a little adjustment. A yoke is a heavy wooden bar for carrying a load, and He wants every one torn off.
The answer is bread. God says His chosen fast is “…to share your bread with the hungry…” (Isaiah 58:7) It's simple and it's hands-on, friends. If you have it, you share it.

The answer is True. God says His chosen fast is “…to bring the poor and homeless into your home…” (Isaiah 58:7) That means a real door opened to a real person. It's personal, friends, and I think that's the point.

The answer is the glory of the LORD. God says “Your righteousness will go before you, and the glory of the LORD will be your rear guard.” (Isaiah 58:8) A rear guard is the one watching your back, friends. So righteousness is out front and the LORD's glory is covering behind.
The answer is answer. God says “Then you will call, and the LORD will answer…” (Isaiah 58:9) They had asked why He didn't notice them. Here He says that when they call, He answers, friends.

The answer is True. God says “If you remove the yoke from your midst, the pointing of the finger and malicious talk, and if you give yourself to the hungry and satisfy the afflicted soul, then your light will go forth in the darkness.” (Isaiah 58:9-10) Both parts of the if come first, friends. Then the light goes out into the dark.
The answer is noonday. God says “…your night will be like noonday.” (Isaiah 58:10) Noon is the brightest part of the day, friends. So the promise is a night that's like the middle of the day.

The answer is a well-watered garden. God says “You will be like a well-watered garden, like a spring whose waters never fail.” (Isaiah 58:11) Picture a garden in a sun-scorched land, friends, and a spring whose waters never fail. That's a lot of comfort in one verse.

The answer is Repairer of the Breach. God says “you will be called Repairer of the Breach, Restorer of the Streets of Dwelling.” (Isaiah 58:12) A breach is a gap or a break, friends. The verse also says they will rebuild the ancient ruins and restore the age-old foundations.

The answer is delight. God says “…if you call the Sabbath a delight, and the LORD’s holy day honorable…” (Isaiah 58:13) He wants it called a delight, friends, which is a whole different feeling from a chore. Then He keeps going with what honoring it looks like.

The answer is False. God says to honor the Sabbath “…by not going your own way or seeking your own pleasure or speaking idle words…” (Isaiah 58:13) So going their own way is the thing to leave behind, friends. It's a sentence full of nots.

The answer is the heritage of their father Jacob. God says “…I will make you ride on the heights of the land and feed you with the heritage of your father Jacob.” (Isaiah 58:14) Jacob is called their father, friends, so this is their own family inheritance. And the verse ends with “For the mouth of the LORD has spoken.” (Isaiah 58:14)
